notes.title: Update: Pixelpart 1.8.0
notes.content: [p]Hello, hope you guys are doing well! This update of Pixelpart is packed with new features![/p][p][/p][h2]Effect triggers[/h2][p]This exiting new feature offers a way to make your effects react to events that happen in your game. For example, suppose you are creating a visual effect for a sci-fi laser weapon that has two stages: A "charging" stage that is active when the user holds down the mouse button and a "fire" stage that is activated by releasing the button. You can model this with [i]triggers[/i] inside Pixelpart: The emission of the particles of the second stage is only done when a trigger is activated.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/4b97c0e720aff0c9bb0c664b953844494003ac91.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]You can use the new [i]Triggers[/i] window to define triggers:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/60cb23a314a12bfe5accea650201c5498258162b.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]These can then be set as the start or stop trigger of particle emitters, force fields etc. A particle emitter only starts emitting particles after its start trigger is activated:[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/5db5a4fdd689cc0602936df4a26d032b7dd8e88b.gif"][/img] [/p][p]Then you can use the scripting API of Pixelpart in [i]Unity[/i] or [i]Godot[/i] to activate the trigger. For example, in [i]Unity[/i] you can do so by calling [i]effect.ActivateTrigger("Fire")[/i].[/p][p][/p][h2]Node system[/h2][p]The node and object system in Pixelpart has been completely overhauled for improved clarity and flexibility. The object browser now features two distinct lists: one for scene nodes (such as particle emitters, force fields, and more) and another for particle types.[/p][p]Nodes now form a fully functional scene graph, with each node supporting translation, rotation, and scale relative to its parent—enabling more precise and hierarchical control over scene elements.[/p][p]Assigning particle types to emitters is easy: Simply drag a particle type from the bottom list and drop it onto a particle emitter in the top list:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/b2968ce347dfc8c3bf9b96e64568f08eec78a7d0.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Conversion tool[/h2][p]If you ever need to convert a large number of effect files to the newest Pixelpart version, this new little tool has you covered. It can be opened from the [i]File[/i] menu by selecting [i]Convert effects...[/i].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/09e8a9bbc81848e607c9ae6cb224ddd56370800c.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Bézier keyframe interpolation[/h2][p]This updates adds a new Bézier interpolation mode for keyframe animation, which allows you to control animations more precisely.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/12eb7429b5274df25c50aab424d421cb09b55c1c.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Other changes[/h2][list][*][p]When importing an image, there is a new option to specify whether the image is in sRGB or linear color space.[/p][/*][*][p]You can now hide and show particles by clicking on the eye icon next to particle types in the object browser.[/p][/*][*][p]Different types of force fields, colliders and light sources can now be converted to one another in the context menu of each node (right-click on node in object browser).[/p][/*][*][p]Improved mesh import dialog.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed bug where adding an effect to another would fail to import effect inputs.[/p][/*][*][p]Improved existing effect presets.[/p][/*][*][p]Added 1 effect preset.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]Plugins[/h2][p]As always, the Unity and Godot plugins have been updated to the latest version. You can download them at [url="https://pixelpart.net/plugins/"]https://pixelpart.net/plugins/[/url].[/p][p][b]Important:[/b] Before using the new plugins, ensure that all your effects are updated to the latest version—using the conversion tool, for example.[/p][p][b]Key changes[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]Effects now include a [i]warm-up time[/i] property, allowing them to initialize before rendering begins. This is especially useful for effects that require a startup phase.[/p][/*][*][p]A new [i]effect scale[/i] property has been introduced to apply a global scale to the entire effect. This replaces the older scale property on the asset/resource level.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where effects played at reduced speed would appear jerky.[/p][/*][*][p][i](Unity)[/i] The Unity plugin now uses a different system for importing effect assets. Previously, [i].ppfx[/i] files were converted to [i].asset [/i]files by the plugin before they could be used as effect assets. This step is no longer necessary - [i].ppfx[/i] file can now be used directly.[/p][/*][*][p][i](Godot)[/i] The Godot plugin now requires Godot 4.3 or higher![/p][/*][*][p][i](Godot) [/i]The [i]PixelpartEffect[/i] node now supports layer masks, the [i]PixelpartEffect2D[/i] node supports visibility layers.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Update: Pixelpart 1.7.2
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

I'm thrilled to share the latest update to Pixelpart, packed with some highly requested features to enhance your workflow!

[h2]Video Export: MP4 and WMV[/h2]

You can now export your visual effects directly to MP4 and WMV formats, making it easier than ever to share your projects across platforms. In addition, I've added the ability to control the playback speed of effects right in the render window. This gives you more flexibility in fine-tuning the export.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/cbcefbf2d7df7ef1652a940535f5b69fa74e3bc6.png[/img]

[i]Note: The new export formats are only available on Windows. On Linux, use the existing exporters for webm or ogv instead.[/i]

[h2]New Effect Presets[/h2]

Plus, I've also added two new pre-built effects!

[i]Magic trail:[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/969a6e1345a19b04afd710543680ed3b4abd260e.gif[/img]

[i]Smoke and sparks:[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/614a755026e1a2fd630f85b2eafdeb6f1eb800df.gif[/img]

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]

[list]
[*]Improved slow-motion behavior of effects
[/list]

In addition, I've added the ability to control the playback speed of effects right in the render window.
Plus, I've also added two new pre-built effects!

Hey guys, I hope you had a great week! After the major release of version 1.7, I have another update for you improving some usability aspects of the editor!

notes.title: Update: Pixelpart 1.7.0
notes.content:
Hope you guys are doing well! I'm finally back with a big update for Pixelpart. Buckle up, this release is packed with new features!

[h2]Mesh particles[/h2]

Apart from sprite and trail particles, Pixelpart now supports mesh particles, which means you can use 3D models as particles in the 3D effects you create. This feature is fully integrated with the updated versions of the game engine plugins. Currently, Pixelpart supports [i]obj[/i] and [i]ply[/i] files, but importers for other file formats like [i]gltf[/i] are planned. Pixelpart also provides more than 50 built-in meshes that you can use for your effects. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/1e56bac44f8a95211992f94b22b50879b4a269a3.gif[/img]

In the editor, you can add these mesh particles via the object browser:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/2497507935c6e28a17d49c8c3d5a16a9a8753a8d.png[/img]

In the settings of the [i]Renderer[/i] property you can then change the rendered mesh:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/49d4bb77df5aab06069b80010658d4c826652700.png[/img]

[h2]HDR rendering system with lighting[/h2]

Complementing the new mesh particles, the rendering system of Pixelpart has been improved and now supports HDR rendering with lighting!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/fc2ebff9734a45e097602e41f41415598cec2ba4.gif[/img]

There is a new node type [i]Light source[/i], which you can place in the scene to illuminate the effect. There are directional lights to model things like sunlight, point lights for lights that is emitted from a point and spot lights that emit light inside a light cone. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/b87539acd178bb951c6e4baaa650cd591025bee4.png[/img]

Make sure the particles in your scene use a [i]Lit[/i] material if you want them to receive lighting. By the way, the lighting system also works in conjunction with the game engine plugins! But be aware that effects are illuminated using the light sources you define in the game engine, not the ones you define in the Pixelpart editor. These light sources are just for rendering the effect in Pixelpart.

[h2]Dynamic effect inputs[/h2]

If you have ever worked with visual effects in game engines, you may have noticed that it can be very hard to make a particle effect react dynamically to the state of the game. For example, you may want to increase or decrease the intensity of a flame effect, which would require you to change individual particle properties like the particle velocity, size etc. with scripts. Very tedious. Defining these kinds of relations should be part of the design process. Ideally, you should be able to define a high-level property [i]Intensity[/i]of the effect and only change the value of this input in a game script. Pixelpart's solution to this problem is dynamic effect inputs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/26d8fce97be682c1442407b36c60282adb2efbb1.gif[/img]

In the new [i]Effect inputs[/i] window, you can add new effect inputs. The relationship between effect inputs and properties of the effect, like the velocity of particles, their color or really anything, can then be defined with visual scripting in the [i]Compute graph[/i] window. When using the effect in game engines, you can then simply set the value of the effect input with simple functions like [i]SetEffectInputFloat("Intensity", 1.0)[/i] and the effect will react accordingly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/8e62dd510d5ad50e54bfa659475157a74edfae74.png[/img]

[h2]Updated material system[/h2]

This release slightly changes the way materials for particles are handled. You can now directly choose from a set of predefined materials in the [i]Visuals[/i] tab of a particle type, which offer many properties for customization and are always supported in the game engine plugins. You can still create completely custom materials using shader graphs by selecting [i]New[/i] in the material dropdown. However, such materials may in some instances not be supported by game engine plugins. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/b07bb15f14888fb560806ff89cffc4271c8aa4f7.png[/img]

[h2]Noise, velocity and drag fields[/h2]

This release adds three new types of force fields:

- The [i]noise field[/i] moves particles using randomly generated noise, which is useful for organic particle motion.
- The [i]vector field[/i] allows you to load a velocity field from file.
- The [i]drag field[/i] simulates drag through air of fluids and can be used to slow down particles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/0639728abfaccd04a1ac2046085ae0f7b4dbf246.gif[/img]

You can add these different force fields in the object browser:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/dfa28c755d90963027ad798f3030aedeb81bbe54.png[/img]

[h2]3D colliders[/h2]

Pixelpart has always had colliders for 2D effects, but now they can be used in 3D as well! The vertices of the collider can be adjusted in the 3D scene view. The new version also introduces a new feature, that allows particles to be killed upon contact with a collider, which can be useful if you have sub-particles that get spawned when a parent particle is killed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/76562ee85384112872139be13818346289d9a17c.gif[/img]

[h2]Grid particle distribution[/h2]

The new release adds two new distribution modes for particles: [i]Grid (random)[/i] and [i]Grid (ordered)[/i]. They can be used to let particles spawn on the points of a grid expanding the variety of effects you can create. The [i]Grid (random)[/i] mode spawns particles at random grid points, while the [i]Grid (ordered)[/i] mode spawns particles one grid point after the other. The number of grid points and the spawn order can be changed in the additional settings of the [i]Distribution[/i] property.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/0f8c160f06078df8ae728c2154baa5aa4be527a4.gif[/img]

[h2]Inherited particle direction[/h2]

Two new direction modes [i]Inherit[/i] and [i]Inherit (inverse)[/i] have been added in Pixelpart 1.7, which allows particles to inherit the (inverse) direction of parent particles or emitters. This makes it easy to let particles shoot off in the opposite direction of the emitter motion like this:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/5fad2adfa464b822759f9dd962181dde2e56c084.gif[/img]

[h2]Camera alignment for trail particles[/h2]

In 3D, trail particles now offer the additional [i]Alignment mode[/i] option [i]Camera[/i] (accessible in the [i]Motion[/i] tab of the particle type), which causes the trail to always face the viewer.

[h2]New particle properties[/h2]

The new release adds several new properties for particles types:

- [i]Stretch[/i]: How much the size of particles increases or decreases based on the particle speed
- [i]Rotation by speed[/i]: How particles rotate based on their speed
- [i]Inherited velocity[/i]: How much speed particles inherit from their parent particle when spawned
- [i]Physical size[/i]: Size of particles during physics calculations

[h2]Hiding individual image effects[/h2]

Pixelpart now offers the option to hide individual image effects in the image effects window:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/423fd09820e48aa943a42ac584faf461a8b14e71.gif[/img]

[h2]Other changes[/h2]

- Recent effects: There is now a new option in the [i]File[/i] menu to load recently opened effects.
- Add effect: You can add entire effect presets to existing effects now with the [i]Add effect[/i] menu option.
- New shortcuts: [i]Del[/i] to delete the selected object and [i]Ctrl+I[/i] to hide/show the selected object and [i]Ctrl+D[/i] to duplicate it.
- Improved export process: The process for rendering and exporting effects to videos, sprite sheets etc. has been improved and optimized.
- New shader graph nodes: This release adds new nodes for shader graphs, which you can use to create custom materials.

notes.title: Roadmap for Pixelpart
notes.content:
Hope you guys are doing well! It's been a few months since I last posted anything, and I would like to update you about the things I'm working on and my vision for Pixelpart. I believe Pixelpart has the potential to be useful to many more game developers and VFX artists. Beginning with the upcoming release of Pixelpart 1.7, I aim to bring Pixelpart to a truly professional level in the context of visual effects in games. Specifically, the changes will include:

[list]
[*] Support for 3D meshes making it possible to use them as  particles
[*] Revision of the rendering system with real-time lighting and HDR rendering
[*] New effect attribute system, which will allow you to define dynamic attributes for your effect and connect them to the basic particle attributes via visual scripting. This is particularly useful for the game engine plugins. Instead of needing to change a lot of particle properties with scripts when you want an effect to react to something in the world, the plugins will then offer a simple method to change a dynamic input, changing all necessary properties as defined in the editor!
[*] New types of force field like noise fields, vector fields and drag fields in both 2D and 3D
[*] Of course, the integration of these new features into the runtime plugins for Unity and Godot
[/list]

A sneak peek of the work-in-progress lighting and rendering system: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/4bd04609110506c9acd3b6217a88911874f057f2.gif[/img]

The new attribute system in action. In this example, a single attribute is used to derive multiple properties of the flame:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/d7767954961986a989846ab5daee8a0541ec89f1.gif[/img]

Right now, I'm in the middle of implementing all of this and plan to be finished in around 3 months. In the meantime, a small bugfix update for Pixelpart 1.6 will be released soon. Once the update to Pixelpart 1.7 is finished, I intend to invest more time into marketing and producing learning material like tutorials and hands-on examples. Additionally, I may develop more runtime plugins, like for UE5, which has been requested quite a lot.

Thank you for supporting Pixelpart!

notes.title: Update: Pixelpart 1.6.3
notes.content:
Lately, I've been really motivated to work on Pixelpart, so here's your next update! By the way, if you haven't joined our [url=https://discord.gg/pAptFvFDAj]community server on Discord[/url] yet, now is the time!

[h2]Snapping for 3D transform tools[/h2]

The new snapping feature is very useful if you're working with 3D effects and use the gizmos for translation, rotation and scaling. Particle emitters and force fields now snap to positions and angles if snapping is enabled.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/426814064b9d3785854c0641c0fab599a0deac06.gif[/img]

[h2]New effect presets[/h2]

This release adds new 3D effect presets for you to use:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/b763f8822b4806505a5929e112bd68a617b84321.gif[/img]  [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/ec9dce09e26e71fc877d6696e57ce7f1fd412eda.gif[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/989f5a705e694a3e2fb77309fd3d8ad563568489.gif[/img]
Black Energy Trails, Fire Ring, Radiating Energy

I've also improved many existing effects!

[h2]Other changes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Improved icon set
[*]Particle trails improved visually
[*]The "New Project" dialog now lets you select whether you want to create a 2D or 3D effect more easily
[*]The "About" dialog now lists third-party software used by Pixelpart
[/list]

notes.title: Update: Pixelpart 1.6.2
notes.content:
Today, I've got a smaller update for you, which focuses on UI improvements and bugfixes!

[h2]Tooltips[/h2]

Sometimes it can be hard to guess what properties of particle emitters, particle types, force fields and colliders actually do. With the new tooltip system, you'll receive helpful tips if you hover over a property's name. Of course, tooltips are localized and available in English, Spanish, German and Simplified Chinese.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/4b685c5e715a932e8acf557e5597f5e3b807e51b.gif[/img]

Tooltips can also be disabled under [i]File > Preferences...[/i].

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Improved material preview in shader graph editor with two different preview modes
[*]Particle distribution property now has different icons for each mode
[*]Fix: Crash for some graphics drivers when loading effects
[*]Fix: Shader compilation errors in shader graph editor
[*]Fix: Issues with file dialogs in shader graph editor
[/list]

notes.title: Update: Pixelpart 1.6.1
notes.content:
I hope you've created some cool new effects with Pixelpart's recent addition of 3D! Today's update focuses on quality-of-life improvements for the editor!

[h2]Dockable Windows[/h2]

You can now easily customize the editor layout with the new dockable windows feature, which allows you to move every window in Pixelpart and dock it anywhere you want:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/ec8cad803af7b06b8907326aa040208858b79f7f.gif[/img]

[h2]Camera Movement Speed[/h2]

There is a new setting to change the movement speed of the camera in 3D, which is useful if you want to move more quickly through your scene:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/a4c7f89e5d9747485681ec62b811c1ce7e705e70.png[/img]

[h2]Node Filter[/h2]

If you create effects with lots of particle types and emitters, it can be complicated to keep track of all the different nodes in your scene. With this update, the object browser allows you to search for nodes: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/d80d0418af326e2e40a9cc593232503a20c6e31c.png[/img]

[h2]Saving & Loading Shader Graphs[/h2]

You can now save and load shader graphs that you have created for your particles, which makes it possible to share shaders between different effects without having to re-create the shader graph:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/963ae4b961af50bfbb0aa3123f3759a281fa50f8.png[/img]

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Zoom with mouse wheel now possible in 3D
[*]New gizmo for force direction and strength of 3D area forces
[*]Improved script editor
[*]Support for larger UI scale
[*]Better performance
[*]Fixed: Rotation issues of particle sprites
[*]Fixed: Crash during export
[/list]

notes.title: Update: Pixelpart 1.6
notes.content:
After some time without new releases, I’m back with a big update: Pixelpart now supports 3D!

[h2]3D Effects[/h2]

Great news! You are now able to create 3D effects in Pixelpart and import them into game engines with the provided runtime plugins for Godot (with support for Godot 4 coming soon) and Unity. Of course they can be rendered to images, sprite sheets and videos as well. Here is how 3D effects look like in Pixelpart:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/7a676cea22f8ca5035f783c426b48d4f7531fcf6.png[/img]

The 3D effects work similarly to 2D effects, but with the addition of a third coordinate for properties like position and size. The new gizmos for translation, rotation, and scaling make it easy to position particle emitters and force fields in your scene, while new emission shapes like spheres, cubes, and cylinders provide even more creative options. To navigate the 3D scene, use WASD while holding the right mouse button.

By the way: If you have an existing 2D effect that you'd like to convert to a 3D effect, simply tick the [i]3D Effect[/i] checkbox in the [i]Edit[/i] menu.

[h2]New Workflow[/h2]

The workflow for creating particle effects has been improved for greater versatility. Instead of having the emitter object define both particle emission and appearance, you can now have a particle emitter be responsible for emitting one or multiple particle types. Previously, having the same emitter emit different types of particles was not possible, but Pixelpart now allows for it. In Pixelpart, an emitter with multiple particle types looks like this:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/705fbcc86786906c3720a0eabe319a2f476c1cba.png[/img]

Don't worry if you have older effects created in previous versions of Pixelpart. They will be automatically converted to the new format when you load them into the new version of Pixelpart.

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]

[list]
[*]There is now a handy timeline below the scene view showing the current time and letting you pause and restart the simulation.
[*]Editing keyframes for vector data (like position, rotation, size) is now possible in a combined multigraph keyframe editor
[*]You can assign custom names to nodes in the shader graph now (right-click on node)
[*]New nodes for the shader graph editor: Value curve, logic nodes
[*]New shader graph presets
[*]New effect presets
[*]New emitter presets
[*]Improved application icon
[/list]

notes.title: Update: Pixelpart 1.5.2
notes.content:
Version 1.5.2 is a small update, mainly improving the user interface.

[h2]Easier Sub-Emitter Creation[/h2]
You can now create sub-emitters of an existing particle emitter directly from the toolbar or the context menu using the new option [i]Add Sub-Emitter[/i]. Before Version 1.5.2, you had to create a normal emitter first and place it below another one with drag & drop.
The name of emitters and other objects can be changed from the context menu as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/4d48a3b5d16eaa5bc54c7917fb777d1292b21f75.png[/img]

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Removed unnecessary buttons to add, duplicate and remove objects below the object list. These actions are already found in the toolbar, context menu (via right-click) and main menu.
[*]New setting [i]Custom Title Bar[/i] to hide the default Windows title bar of the application (enabled by default).
[/list]

notes.title: Update: Pixelpart 1.5.1
notes.content:
Version 1.5.1 of Pixelpart has been released!

[h2]New Language: Chinese (中文)[/h2]
[i]Pixelpart[/i] is now available in Simplified Chinese! To change the language open the preferences via [i]File > Preferences...[/i] in the main menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/caba5145ebed8053d96086008283f25d8d30c9a2.png[/img]

[h2]Size Controls[/h2]
You can now adjust the size of emission areas, force fields and images directly on the effect preview by moving the small knobs at the edge.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/92d2ab44ddc5ec919f1a8ccf89e2b70910d30add.png[/img]

[h2]Effect Templates[/h2]
With the new release, there is an option to create a new project from an effect template. In the [i]New Project[/i] dialog, select the effect you want to start from in the drop-down menu. There are 18 different templates for you to choose. Of course, you can still create effects from scratch.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/452bd7fbb15a5ab080bba6e7ca48ae7b8d736f95.png[/img]

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*]New option to add vertices to an existing collider by selecting it in the list and then clicking on the effect while holding [i]Ctrl[/i]

notes.title: Update: Pixelpart 1.5
notes.content:
Version 1.5 of [i]Pixelpart[/i] has been released with several new features: Shader graphs, custom spawn paths, unlimited sub-emitters and auto-cropping!

[h2]Shader Graphs[/h2]
In previous versions, adjusting the appearance of particles was limited to changing their sprite texture and color. With this release, you can now use [i]shader graphs[/i] to define the material of particles more precisely. You can make materials react dynamically to particle properties like speed, for example. Such a shader graph consists of nodes that work together to define the final pixel color and opacity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/ba6d32fdc2a1db621ed5f9692d3a88fadceec8c6.png[/img]

[h2]Custom Spawn Paths[/h2]
A new type of spawn shape for custom paths has been added. Using this type, you can define custom spawn paths for particles by choosing waypoints directly on the effect preview. Simply select the new [i]Path[/i] shape in the [i]General[/i] options and choose waypoints by right-clicking on the effect preview.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/6f9a764f3720a2315d3141936729ec7accac2143.png[/img]

[h2]Unlimited Sub-Emitters[/h2]
It is now easier than ever to spawn particles from other particles. You drag the emitter that should spawn particles in relation to another emitter onto that emitter in the list of objects. It will become a [i]sub-emitter[/i] of the latter. This release adds the possibility to have an unlimited number of sub-emitters for each emitter, not just one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41556781/e93e7541a58dac9504f2e10834604368557d00c8.png[/img]

[h2]Auto-Cropping for Final Render[/h2]
This release introduces [i]auto-cropping[/i] for the final render. After selecting the new option in the render dialog, the rendering process automatically fits the effect into the frame of the rendered video.

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*]New option to adjust the grid spacing in the keyframe editor
[*]The Windows version now has a custom window title bar
[/list]

notes.title: Update: Pixelpart 1.4.2
notes.content:
Version 1.4.2 of [i]Pixelpart[/i] has been released, adding web support and a billboard mode to the plugins and improving the [i]Pixelpart[/i] editor.

[h2]Plugins: Billboard Mode[/h2]
Although effects created in [i]Pixelpart[/i] are 2D and thus primarily used in 2D games, they can be quite useful for 3D as well. For this to work well, they need to be oriented towards to the camera to not break the illusion (billboard rendering). With this update this mode is now integrated into the plugins and can be activated for an effect by enabling the "Billboard" mode.

[h2]Plugins: Web Support[/h2]
The plugins for Unity and Godot finally support HTML5/WebGL, which means you can now use effects created in [i]Pixelpart[/i] in your web games!

[h2]Keyframe Editor: Snapping[/h2]
The keyframe editor now offers a snapping option, which makes it possible to modify the timing of keyframes much more precisely. The feature can be enabled in the menu above the keyframe editor. Right now the resolution of the snapping grid is fixed, but future versions will allow you to adjust it.

[h2]Particle Trails: Sprite Sheet Animation[/h2]
The trail renderer has been improved with animated particle trails! Like particle sprites, trails can now be textured with animated sprite sheets. 

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*]The layout of the user interface has updated, for example actions for the selected scene object are now located below the object list. 
[*]The collision solver has been improved to prevent particles from tunneling through colliders.
[*]Bug fixes regarding particle motion paths.
[/list]

notes.title: Update: Pixelpart 1.4.1
notes.content:
This update adds new export options, expands the capabilities of the trail renderer and improves loop rendering.

[h2]New Formats for Video Export[/h2]
This update adds two new formats for video export:
[list]
[*][i]avi[/i]
[*][i]webm[/i]
[/list]
Videos in [i]webm[/i] format even support alpha transparency, suitable for effects with transparent background.

[h2]Better Trail Renderer[/h2]
The trail renderer for particles has been updated: Instead of only one trail per emitter, each parent particles generates its own trail while its moving. This lets you create even more diverse effects (for example, see the newly added effect "Electric").

[h2]Improved Loop Rendering[/h2]
In previous version rendering effects as continuous loops did not work well in some cases, especially for effects with many emitter. This feature has been greatly improved, allowing most effects to be rendered in a perfect loop.

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Support for palette files created with Paint.NET.
[*]Improved keyframe editor.
[*]A key symbol now marks properties of emitters and other objects that are animated with keyframes.
[*]Input fields for rotation values now have a small widget showing the selected angle.
[*]Force fields are now shown moving on their motion path if a path is specified.
[*]Theme "Light" for the user interface has been improved.
[*]New effect examples and emitter presets.
[*]Existing effects have been updated.
[*]Translations to Spanish and German have been updated.
[*]Rendering bugs in the plugins have been fixed.
[/list]

notes.title: Update: Pixelpart 1.4
notes.content:
The new version of [i]Pixelpart[/i] is finally here! I am happy to announce the release of version 1.4, which offers a ton of new features and possibilities.

[h2]Plugins for Unity and Godot 3[/h2]
You can now play effects you created in [i]Pixelpart[/i] directly inside game engines using the new runtime plugins for Unity and Godot 3, instead of relying on sprite sheets or image sequences. The plugins let you modify an effect and individual particle emitters, force fields and colliders dynamically from script, even while the effect is playing. You can find further information on how to install and use the plugins in the documentation included with [i]Pixelpart[/i]. Note, however, that only Windows, Linux, and macOS are supported as of version 1.4. If you want to ship to consoles, mobile or web, it is recommended to still use sprite sheets or image sequences. Support for more platform is going to come in the future. If you find any instances, where the plugins don't function properly, please report them in the community hub under "Bug Reports"!
The plugins are available at [url=https://soeren-m.itch.io/pixelpart]Itch.io: Pixelpart[/url]. A short guide on how to install and use the plugins can be found in the documentation (Help menu in [i]Pixelpart[/i]).

[h2]Video Export[/h2]
With this release it is now possible to export effects as videos! The video is encoded with the royalty-free video codec Theora inside an ogv file. Supporting other common video codecs and formats like the H.264 codec (commonly used in mp4 files) is a bit tricky, because they are patent-encumbered and come with license fees. For now, I have decided to not include any proprietary or patent-encumbered codecs and stick to the Theora codec. Support for other formats is planned for future updates.

[h2]Animated PNG Export[/h2]
In order to place an effect on a web page, effects can be exported as GIFs, but the GIF format lacks several desirable features like partial transparency. This release adds the option to export effects as animated PNG files (.apng), which are like GIF files, but support 24 bit colors and partial transparency. They are supported by most major web browsers.

[h2]Trail Renderer for Particles[/h2]
Sometimes it is useful to not render each particle as an individual sprite, but to combine them to a single, continuous trail (think of sword slashes and lighting bolts for example). The new trail renderer is suited for these exact situations.

[h2]Better Force Fields & Colliders[/h2]
Force fields and colliders have experienced a major revision. In previous versions they were always part of an emitter. This was problematic: To let a force field or collider affect multiple emitters, it had to be copied to every emitter, which was tedious. Now, they are their own object type and, by default, affect every emitter, but you still can exclude specific emitters if needed. Further updates:
[list]
[*]New randomization for force fields that uses a grid with variable size, where each grid cell has a slightly different force direction and strength
[*]Better collider physics, which allows particles to properly slide down colliders
[*]New fiction property controlling the sliding behavior
[*]Multi-line colliders, so creating complex collision shapes is easier[/list]

[h2]New Particle Emitter Settings[/h2]
In previous versions, particle emitters were inflexible in some situations. For example, it was not directly possible to let an emitter produce particles with a time-dependent initial opacity, only the opacity over a particle's lifetime could be adjusted. The release adds the following properties to allow for more complex effects:
[list]
[*]Initial particle velocity
[*]Initial particle size
[*]Initial particle opacity
[*]Initial particle rotation
[*]Variance for angular velocity[/list]

[h2]Static Sprites[/h2]
It was only possible to include a single background image In previous versions. The new version of [i]Pixelpart[/i] allows you to add an arbitrary amount of sprites, which can even be moved on motion paths or animated with sprite sheet animations.

[h2]Post-Processing Effects[/h2]
Existing post-processing effects have been improved and a lot of useful effects have been added:
[list]
[*]Invert
[*]Grayscale
[*]Contrast-Brightness
[*]Hue-Saturation
[*]Gamma Correction
[*]Colorize
[*]Color Curves
[*]Film Grain
[*]Bilateral Filter
[*]Kuwahara Filter[/list]

[h2]Localization[/h2]
Translations for the following languages have been added:
[list]
[*]Spanish
[*]German
[/list]
The language can be set in the application's preferences. Although the interface has been translated with care, the translations may not be perfect, so if you are proficient in one of those languages and think that the text of a button, a menu option or other elements sounds wrong, please report this in the community hub under "Bug Reports". Translations into other languages are planned.
The software is also now able to display Japanese, Korean and Simplified Chinese characters correctly. Entering names for emitters etc. with those characters is still buggy, however.

[h2]Open-Source Runtime Library[/h2]
The runtime library (implemented in C++) that is used to simulate particle effects in [i]Pixelpart[/i] is released as open source at [url=https://github.com/soeren-m/pixelpart-runtime]GitHub: pixelpart-runtime[/url]. If you have a custom game engine, you can integrate this library to load and simulate effects you have created in [i]Pixelpart[/i] directly in your game engine.
Similarly, the source code for plugins is open source and available at [url=https://github.com/soeren-m/pixelpart-plugin-unity]GitHub: pixelpart-plugin-unity[/url] and [url=https://github.com/soeren-m/pixelpart-plugin-godot3]GitHub: pixelpart-plugin-godot3[/url].

[h2]Other Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*]New effect examples and emitter presets.
[*]Effect examples can now be previewed in the main menu.
[*]Optimized particle rendering.
[*]Graphs, motion paths and gradients can now be copy-pasted.
[*]Pan and zoom available for the graph editor.
[*]The file dialog now offers the option to show/hide hidden files and adds buttons for zooming in and out.
[*]Bug fixes regarding the file explorer.
[*]The Help menu now shows a link to the documentation.
[*]Some other general improvements to the user interface.[/list]
